clue.text: Records number of delays, switching 14 repeatedly

indicators.note: 14 across is the phrase 'right to left', read as an instruction to change R into L, done more than once here

parts.note: to delay is to tarry, so delays (verb) gives the third-person form

explanation.surface: A clerk logs how many hold-ups occurred while a rule is applied over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme entries are instructions: 14 (right to left) means turn R into L. Both Rs of the synonym for delays become Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies as a verb means keeps a count or reckons up, much as one records figures.

clue.text: Most of the career for singer

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter, so the word is cut short

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned most of a career to become a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to speed. The bird is the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, so in crossword terms it is a singer.

clue.text: All the disruption could be deadly

indicators.note: disruption throws the letters into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Any disruption at all might prove fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal and deadly are synonyms, both meaning capable of causing death.

clue.text: Livid about libertine's first lechery, to give an example

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the angry word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: livid means furious, irate

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word libertine

parts.note: lechery is lust

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a rake's first lewdness offers a case in point.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate is to clarify with an example or picture.

clue.text: Rice dishes — some impress us highly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic says certain rice dishes really wow us.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese vinegared rice served with fish or vegetables, so it is a rice dish.

clue.text: Mixing device that appears when pianist 11

indicators.note: 11 across is 'swaps sides', taken as an order to trade the left-hand L and the right-hand R letters

parts.note: Alfred Brendel is a celebrated Austrian concert pianist

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is said to materialise whenever a famous musician changes allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: Exchanging the R and the L in the pianist's surname (RENDEL becomes LENDER) gives the gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is a kitchen appliance that purées and combines ingredients.

clue.text: Guest band wrecked house in Berlin

indicators.note: wrecked means broken up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A visiting band trashed a property in the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a legislative chamber, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is the lower parliamentary chamber of Germany, which sits in Berlin.

clue.text: In Latin I can introduce syllogiser's conclusion

definitions.text: In Latin I can introduce syllogiser's conclusion

parts.words: In Latin I can introduce syllogiser's conclusion
parts.note: the Latin word for therefore, which introduces the conclusion of a syllogism

explanation.walkthrough: A syllogism ends 'therefore ...', and the Latin word for therefore is the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, the word that introduces a logical conclusion.

clue.text: I am interrupting to stop bore

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so I and AM go inside the other word

parts.note: to deter is to stop or prevent
taken as written, the letters I and AM

explanation.surface: Someone cuts in to silence a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a tedious person but the width of a gun barrel or tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The bore of a gun or pipe is its internal width measured across.

clue.text: Respond sympathetically with tears one faked

indicators.note: faked means made up or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows sympathy with crocodile tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas that resonate strike a chord, evoking a shared feeling.

clue.text: 26 11 for this Afro-Asian animal

indicators.note: 11 across is 'swaps sides', taken as an order to trade the L and R letters in the word given

parts.note: 26 refers to the solution of 26 across, meaning 'in time'

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue pointing to a creature found in Africa and Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L and R of the 26-across answer: its first letter L becomes R and its last letter R becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce mammal native to Africa and southern Asia.

clue.text: Timer in seaside plant, having transformed 14

indicators.note: 14 across is 'right to left', read as an instruction to change an R into an L

parts.note: sand grass is a coarse grass growing on coastal dunes

explanation.surface: A dune grass has somehow become a kitchen clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the R in the dune grass to L.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass filled with sand measures a fixed period, so it serves as a timer.

clue.text: Converts 14 and 18, producing defects

definitions.meaning: turns right into left and left into right, i.e. trades one side for the other
a defector changes allegiance from one camp to the opposing one

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: changing right to left and left to right is trading sides; the second is the political sense of switching camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who defects abandons their party and joins the opposition, changing allegiance.

clue.text: Tacked, for example, after turning 22 — that's understood

indicators.note: 22 across is 'west to east', read as an instruction to change a W into an E

parts.note: tacking is a loose kind of stitching, so tacked is an example of sewn

explanation.surface: A sailor tacks east and notes that the point has been grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the W of the stitching word to E. 'That's understood' defines the past participle: it has been seen, i.e. grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen can mean grasped or comprehended, as in 'I've seen the point'.

clue.text: Financial manager's short story about revolutionary movement, right?

indicators.note: about means around, so the story word encloses the movement

parts.note: a conte is a short story, from the French
a roll is a turning, rotating movement

explanation.surface: A finance chief has written a short tale about a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics but just means rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: A controller is the official who oversees an organisation's accounts and finances.

clue.text: Some politicians as seen by others, going west …

definitions.text: Some politicians as seen by others
definitions.meaning: the political Right, viewed by those on the Left
on a map west lies to the left, so heading west is moving leftward

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading pairs the political wings; the second is the map direction.
explanation.definitionFit: On a conventional map, travelling westward means moving leftward across the page.

clue.text: Brings in to store outside modern centre — their business is growing

indicators.note: outside means the storing word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to garner is to gather in and store, as a harvest

indicators.note: centre takes the middle two letters of the word modern

explanation.surface: A firm stockpiles goods around a modern hub, its trade expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing' reads as business expansion but means cultivating plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulturists cultivate plants, so raising things is literally their trade.

clue.text: Kind of alcohol that gets clergy drunk — nothing left at the end

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters of clergy are jumbled

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A spirit that leaves the priests tipsy, with nothing left by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end' places O and L after the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerine is chemically an alcohol, having three hydroxyl groups.

clue.text: Suffer badly in work — checks for fit before proceeding

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit inside the word for work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: badly means in a poor way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suffers at their job while trying things on before going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: To offer up a part is to hold it in position to test the fit before fixing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftspeople offer up a piece by holding it in place to check alignment before fixing.

clue.text: … and the opposite, remaining to make amends

parts.note: something remaining is left over
to make amends is to put things right, set right a wrong

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone stays behind to apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition continues 14 across: the opposite of right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversing the previous direction, moving from the left side to the right is its opposite.

clue.text: Liberal welcomed by Democrats, say? Not altogether

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Democrats are an example of a political party

explanation.surface: A Liberal joins the Democrats, but only in some respects.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means to some extent, so not completely.

clue.text: Kept in reserve, held by journalist or editor

indicators.note: held by means the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A news report sat on by a journalist or editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored means put away and saved for future use.

clue.text: Sounded triumphant, having finally amended 22 for some Americans

indicators.note: 22 across is 'west to east', telling us to change a W, here the last letter, into an E

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast in triumph

explanation.surface: A victor cheered after altering a direction for the benefit of certain Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the final W of the boasting word to E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people of Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Like our writing? That's not how global revolution happens

definitions.text: Like our writing? That's not how global revolution happens

parts.words: Like our writing? That's not how global revolution happens
parts.note: English script runs from the left to the right, which on a map runs from one compass point to the opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Western script runs left to right, which on a map is the same as moving from one compass point towards its opposite; the second sentence plays with the idea of the planet's rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: On a north-up map, left corresponds to one compass bearing and right to its opposite, so left-to-right writing travels the same way.

clue.text: Shell international area

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A test zone used for military shelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test (match) is an international game between national sides in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Testa is the biological term for the hard outer coat of a seed.

clue.text: Graves, for example, that might be put in vault

definitions.text: Graves, for example, that might be put in vault

parts.words: Graves, for example, that might be put in vault
parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux red or white kept in a cellar vault, not a burial place

explanation.walkthrough: Graves and vault suggest a cemetery, but Graves is a Bordeaux district and the vault is a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux appellation producing red and white bottles stored in cellars.

clue.text: Result of lacking practice and vigour, initially changing 18

indicators.note: 18 across is 'left to right', telling us to change the first letter L into R

parts.note: vigour is lustiness, robust energy

explanation.surface: Being out of practice and losing vigour leaves you a bit stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the opening L of the word for vigour to R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustiness is the stiffness or loss of skill that comes from neglecting practice.

clue.text: 9 11 in time

indicators.note: 11 across is 'swaps sides', taken as an order to trade the R and L letters in the word given

parts.note: 9 refers to the solution of 9 across, the Afro-Asian animal

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue for something that will happen eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R and L of the 9-across animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent point, so it happens in time, eventually.

clue.text: Comes down, having altered 14 and 18 — they wrap things up

indicators.note: 18 across is 'left to right', so the final L of the abseiling word becomes R
14 across is 'right to left', so the opening R of the abseiling word is altered to L

parts.note: to rappel is to abseil, coming down a rope

explanation.surface: A climber descends a cliff face and changes direction both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first R and the final L of the abseiling word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapper is one who laps, i.e. wraps or folds material around something.

clue.text: Put in order, made easier with 18 alterations

indicators.note: 18 across is 'left to right', here applied twice so both Ls become Rs

parts.note: to allay is to ease or relieve

explanation.surface: Things are tidied and simplified after a few changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ls of the easing word become Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrayed means set out in an orderly arrangement, such as troops drawn up.
